verdict: A credible profile with a strong local reputation and a usable call path, but it gives a ready customer too few ways to act and no observable after-hours or attribution path.

leaks.title: No direct booking action on the profile
leaks.what: No appointment action is visible. The website has a contact form, not a scheduler.
leaks.evidence: The public profile exposes phone and website actions only.
leaks.why: A ready customer must leave Google, find a form, and wait instead of booking.
leaks.fix: Add one branded, working booking action, or state that booking is by phone.

leaks.title: After-hours demand has no observable next step
leaks.what: Hours end at 19:00 with no after-hours policy. The site says to call but does not say who answers.
leaks.evidence: No after-hours message or urgent path is visible on the profile or destination.
leaks.why: An 8pm emergency cannot tell whether calling reaches anyone.
leaks.fix: State the after-hours policy and connect it to one usable path.

leaks.title: Speed-to-lead for profile-origin inquiries is unknown
leaks.what: Public data shows the action, not what happened after the customer called or clicked.
leaks.evidence: Call answer rate, response time, and booking conversion are not public.
leaks.why: A booked job depends on a human response, not only a profile action.
leaks.fix: Measure median response time for profile-origin leads.

strengths: The primary phone is present, usable, and consistent between the profile and the destination.
The profile resolves over HTTPS and lands on the correct business website.
The rating is strong at 4.6 across 38 reviews, with service-specific proof in the review sample.
The service-area configuration is appropriate for a plumbing business without a storefront.

fixes.fix: Add one direct booking action with a branded, working destination
Publish the after-hours policy and connect it to one action
Respond to every review, starting with the recent negative
Add a consistent source parameter to the profile website action
Complete the profile service list and align it with the website

fixNote: The booking action and after-hours line remove the two clearest dead ends in the ready-to-act path. Review replies and source attribution make the existing demand visible. None of these fixes requires a new website.

journey.summary: The business, phone, website, and service-area model are coherent.
Plumbing and drain work are clear; one major service and important attributes are missing.
A strong rating and recent-enough reviews are weakened by no visible owner responses.
Call works; booking is absent; after-hours friction is the main act-stage gap.
The website resolves over HTTPS and matches the business; mobile first action and source context are weak.
Call answer rate and speed-to-lead are not observable from public data.
Booking conversion cannot be measured from the public profile.
Profile-origin revenue and close rate require authorized CRM data.
The public result is visible; the request process is not.
No source parameter distinguishes profile traffic; the destination URL is stable.

ownerData.title: Speed-to-lead
ownerData.why: The profile can produce a call or click; only the phone and CRM systems can show how fast a human responds.
questions: What is the median time from a profile-origin call or form to first human contact?
Does the answer or callback process change after 7pm?

ownerData.title: Booking conversion
ownerData.why: A booking action would create a path; it would not prove that ready customers complete it.
questions: What share of profile-origin booking attempts become scheduled jobs?
Where do customers abandon the current contact form?

ownerData.title: Profile-origin revenue
ownerData.why: Only authorized CRM and financial data can connect profile activity to booked revenue.
questions: Which closed jobs originated from the profile?
What is the average job value and close rate for profile-origin leads?

opportunities.label: Online estimate requests
opportunities.why: The profile expects a ready customer but offers only a generic website contact form; a scoped estimate path could fit larger jobs.

opportunities.label: Review request automation
opportunities.why: Reviews are recent enough to trust but owner responses are absent and review velocity is uneven.

opportunities.label: Profile-origin attribution
opportunities.why: No observable source parameter distinguishes profile traffic from other channels.

opportunities.label: Missed-call recovery
opportunities.why: Call is the primary action; owner data is needed to know whether calls are missed.

opportunities.label: Emergency routing
opportunities.why: Emergency plumbing is advertised but after-hours coverage is not explained.

limitations: Public mode cannot observe call answer rate, speed-to-lead, booking conversion, close rate, or revenue.
The Places API does not expose the complete services list, all attributes, owner responses, posts, or every action type. Those were reviewed from the synthetic public-profile fixture.
Service-area boundaries are not fully exposed by the public Places API.
Only a small public review sample was available; theme and recency analysis is illustrative, not a census.
Connected performance diagnostics are not part of the public score.
nextSteps: This week: add a direct booking action or state plainly that booking is by phone, and publish the after-hours policy.
Next week: respond to every review, starting with the January 2026 negative, and add a source parameter to the profile website action.
Before more ad spend: pull speed-to-lead and profile-origin booking data, then fix the slowest human response step.

findings.fix: Add one direct booking action with a branded destination.

findings.observed: Hours end at 19:00 with no after-hours explanation or path.
findings.fix: State the after-hours policy and connect it to one action.

findings.observed: No owner responses are visible despite 38 reviews.
No recent relevant owner response is visible.
findings.fix: Write specific replies, starting with the recent negative.

findings.observed: The website action has no source parameter.
Leak detection and repiping are on the website but absent from the profile.
Profile and destination service lists differ on leak detection and repiping.
findings.fix: Align the profile and website service list.

findings.observed: No practical attributes are visible beyond the category labels.
findings.fix: Add verified emergency and service-area attributes.

findings.observed: Only one recent media item is visible.
findings.fix: Add a small number of recent job photos.

findings.observed: The handoff preserves no observable source context.
findings.fix: Preserve one source parameter through the handoff.

footer: Synthetic example for documentation. Not a real business. Prepared with GBP Scorecard v1.
executiveSummary: Acme Plumbing has the foundations: a coherent identity, a usable phone path, a correct service-area configuration, and a 4.6 rating across 38 reviews.
The biggest observable conversion gap is the absence of a booking action, followed by an unexplained after-hours experience.
Public data cannot show whether calls are answered or how quickly, so speed-to-lead is an owner-data question, not a score penalty.
The highest-leverage fixes are small: one booking action, one after-hours line, consistent review replies, and one source parameter.
evidenceNote: This is a synthetic documentation example. Evidence strings are illustrative, not a real business record. A real run keeps raw observations in .audit/ and publishes only synthetic or approved sanitized examples.
